newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle turn active $65 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle turn active $65 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales turned active late Friday at $65.00 per cwt, steady with thin sales Wednesday and Thursday, but down $1.00 from light activity on Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
About 25,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma following weekly sales of about 29,000. Kansas sales totalled about 15,000 head following weekly movement near 37,000, they said.
Packers had bid $65.00 most of the week, but were rebuffed by owners holding out for $66.00 to $67.00 because many owners would start losing money at $65.00, the sources said.

Fed cattle prices next week could be pressured further by a carryover of supplies from this week's showlists and by talk that packers would be able to pull from contract cattle supplies when they come due Sunday, feedlot sources said.
Up to this week, feedlots have been current by pulling cattle ahead to meet strong packer demand.
By not selling many cattle this week, feedlots no longer are pulling cattle ahead but will be selling them when they are due to come out, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter.
"In effect, they've lost their currentness," Benson said.
